blocks.what_we_do:
Download and extract the whole source project from its GitHub branch. Then download the matching encrypted data archive from release `data-2026.1`. Follow these actions for the project:

1. Open the GitHub page of the course branch that your instructor gives you. GitHub is a website that stores project files. A branch is one line of versions of a project.
2. Click the green "Code" button. Then click "Download ZIP".
3. Extract the ZIP file into a folder where you can save files, for example in Documents. Use the same method as at step 0.4.
4. Open the extracted folder. You should see the files `config.R` and `GWAS_training_session.Rproj`, and folders such as `R`, `lessons` and `scripts`.

Keep the whole folder together. Do not move single files out of it.

The encrypted data are published in [GitHub Release data-2026.1](https://github.com/mgentiluomo/GWAS_training_session/releases/tag/data-2026.1). The download URLs and SHA-256 checksums are set in `config.R`. The package contains 108 files.
blocks.why: The source project contains code and text. The encrypted package contains the data. A [checksum](../docs/glossary.md#checksum) is a short code calculated from a file. If the file changes, the code changes. Checksums detect changed or damaged downloads. The password decrypts the archive. A correct password does not replace the checksum check.
blocks.you_need:
The complete project folder, R and an internet connection. The command below downloads `course-data-2026.1.zip` and its small manifest file, `MANIFEST.tsv`, for you.

Request the password with your university email through the [data access form](https://www.manuelgentiluomo.it/teaching/gwas/data-access). In class, you can scan the QR code to open the same form. The form sends the password automatically only to addresses ending in `@unipi.it` or `@studenti.unipi.it`. Other users should write to [manuel.gentiluomo@unipi.it](mailto:manuel.gentiluomo@unipi.it). The password changes every academic year. Do not share it. It never appears in the repository or on the site.
blocks.command:
Run the following commands in the RStudio console after you open the project. If you have not opened it yet, do step 0.6 first and then return here. The commands do not run automatically when this notebook is rendered:

```{r s0-5_data, eval=FALSE}
source("R/package_setup.R")
install_course_packages()
source("R/course.R")
download_course_data()
```

The first run of `install_course_packages()` can take several minutes and print many lines. Wait until the `>` prompt returns.

Local fallback: if you already have the published ZIP and its `MANIFEST.tsv`, use this command instead of the download command above. It reads the archive from your computer and makes no network download. Replace the text in quotes with the place where you saved the ZIP file. Write the path with forward slashes (/), also on Windows:

```{r s0-5_local, eval=FALSE}
download_course_data(
  zip_path = "C:/Users/yourname/Downloads/course-data-2026.1.zip"
)
```

For the local fallback, `MANIFEST.tsv` must be in the same folder as the ZIP file. The function `download_course_data` uses `getPass` to ask for a masked password. A prompt asks for the password. Type it and press Enter. You will not see the letters appear. Do not write the password in this notebook, in a shared script or in your command history. Students have no separate terminal command to decrypt the archive. Both routes use the same R helper and the `archive` package. You do not need to install 7-Zip.
blocks.expected_result: R prints `Course data are ready: 108 files verified.` The data are in the folder `data/course/`. The archive and its small manifest file (a list of the files inside) must both match their configured SHA-256 values. R also checks every extracted data file.
blocks.troubleshooting: If R says that the release is not configured, download the current course project again. If the download fails, check your internet connection. You can use the local fallback with files from the published release. If the password is wrong, R shows a message that asks you to check your typing and to contact the instructor if needed. Never bypass a checksum failure. If the destination folder already exists, R refuses to continue. This protects your work. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).
blocks.quick_check:
If the checksum differs but the password is accepted, should you use that download?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>No. Obtain the approved matching package before continuing.</details>
blocks.files_created: Verified data in `data/course/`. R removes the temporary download and extraction files. Data and passwords are never added to Git.
